lesson_title: R9 In, R13 Out: How a Spaza Shop Makes Money
hook_text: She buys a cooldrink for R9 and sells it for R13. So why isn't the R4 all profit?
clip_script: Monday: Mama Thembi buys 24 cans at the cash-and-carry. R9 each, that is the cost price. She sells them for R13 each, the selling price. Mark-up: R4 a can. All 24 sold: R312 in, R216 out, R96 gross profit. But wait: R40 for the taxi, plus electricity for the fridge. Those come out too. And she can't just charge R20, because next door sells for R12. Competition, customers and costs decide the price. She didn't make the cooldrink. She made it convenient. That is trading.
visual_style: A whiteboard spaza shop with a tray of cans, price tags flipping from R9 to R13, and coins dropping into in and out piles.
pacing: Quick number build, a twist on costs, then a calm explanation.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out the mark-up on three things sold near your home.
